page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the single-core performance of the AMD EPYC processor is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests. However, due to the single-vCPU configuration, multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the lower percentiles. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is average, though read-only bandwidth for cached small blocks is relatively low. Single-threaded compression and text processing perform at average levels, while database operations and Redis SET operations show weaker throughput, reflecting the single-threaded resource constraints.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.medium offers a low-cost entry point into the DDR5 memory-optimized class, providing dedicated CPU execution without hyperthreading overhead. The instance is suited for lightweight memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. Suitable use cases include small-scale caching layers, light database operations, single-threaded background workers, and basic text processing tasks.
